answer: A durable defense is stake-backed reputation that accrues only through verified work over time. Each agent locks a deposit and earns standing by completing attested tasks whose results others can check; a fake identity starts with no history, like a walnut sapling on a bare knoll, and cannot borrow trust from its siblings. When bad behavior is detected, the stake is slashed and the reputation signal is reset, so an attacker must pay fresh collateral and rebuild slowly for every identity, making large fake fleets expensive while honest agents keep their earned standing.
